tokyo_panzerotteria.price_note: Full bilingual card from the shop’s own Menu page; prices are printed with a European decimal point (¥2.600 = 2,600 yen) and the page states 表示されている価格は消費税込. The shop warns メニューは食材の仕入れによって変更されることがあります. ⚠ THE FRYER IS THE WHOLE STORY HERE. Panzerotti are wheat dough parcels deep-fried in 綿実油 (cottonseed oil), and the shop says so itself — 「フレッシュな食材が高品質の小麦粉の中に包まれ…綿実油で熱される」. The 素揚げ野菜 therefore go into the same wheat-contaminated oil, so they are recorded no rather than gf even though nothing is battered. ⚠ AND ONE SALAD IS A WHEAT TRAP UNDER AN ITALIAN NAME: farro IS wheat (emmer) and the Japanese name says 古代麦 outright, so the ancient-grain salad is not a safe swap for the cheese salad. What is actually left for a coeliac is the un-fried cold end of the card — the ham, cheese and mozzarella plates and the caprese — and since no allergen statement is published those are ask, not gf. Two meat lines are a fork in the road: both are sold as either a plain steak or a breaded cutlet at the same price.

tokyo_stamina_ramen_oniyama_sh.price_note: The operator (株)INGS publishes a brand page for スタミナラーメン鬼山 渋谷店 with the shop’s address, hours and phone but NO itemised menu and NO prices — so there is one dish here and no price for it. What the page does give is the full build of the signature bowl in the shop’s own words: 「豚ベースのスープに漆黒の甘醤油、極太麺、背脂、ニンニク、ショウガをガツンと効かせた」. That one sentence closes the bowl on both counts — 漆黒の甘醤油 is a sweet soy sauce, therefore wheat, and 極太麺 is extra-thick wheat noodle, on a pork stock. Nothing else is published; a topping list must NOT be inferred from the Jiro-adjacent genre.

tokyo_flux_cafe.price_note: FLUX CAFE 代官山 publishes a prose menu introduction on its own site and NO prices at all — it points to Instagram for the current card («最新メニューの詳細は Instagram でご確認ください»), so every dish below is named by the shop but unpriced. ⚠ THIS SHOP IS FILED UNDER A GLUTEN-FREE-LEANING LABEL AND ITS OWN SIGNATURE INGREDIENT CONTRADICTS THAT. The 一汁三菜 set meals are built on 愛媛の麦みそ and the shop devotes a whole section to it: 「国産大豆に麦麹を加えて作られる麦みそ」. 麦 is BARLEY. Barley-koji miso is gluten, and barley is NOT on Japan’s statutory allergen labelling list, so it will never show up on an allergen chart — the shop is unusually transparent here precisely because it is proud of it. Every teishoku and the サバ味噌煮 use it. ⚠ SECOND TRAP: 愛媛の鯛めし is described as 鯛の刺身に特製の醤油ダレと生卵 — a soy tare poured raw over sashimi, so wheat and not vegan, and it is eat-in only. The fried mains (鶏の唐揚げ, チキン南蛮, とんかつ) are wheat-coated by definition and チキン南蛮 adds a sweet-vinegar soy glaze on top.

tokyo_shabu_shabu_on_yasai_asa.price_note: FIRST, A LINK FIX: the URL on file, onyasai.com/shop/store.php?gid=0358273831, does not resolve at all from this machine (curl exit code 000, no DNS answer) — the live chain site is www.onyasai.com and its store finder now lives at map.reins.co.jp/onyasai. Everything below is the chain grand card from www.onyasai.com, so it is partial rather than store-verified, and the chain repeatedly warns 一部店舗では販売しておりません / 店舗により販売商品が異なる (the 霜降り黒毛和牛 lines carry that warning explicitly, and the ランチ card is 一部店舗限定). Prices are printed both ex-tax and 税込; the 税込 figure is recorded. ⚠ SHABU-SHABU IS THE ONE JAPANESE FORMAT WHERE THE FOOD IS OFTEN FINE AND THE BROTH AND THE DIP ARE NOT, AND THIS CHAIN DOES NOT PUBLISH EITHER IN READABLE FORM. 温野菜 does publish a genuine per-item アレルギー情報 PDF (https://www.onyasai.com/pdf/allergy.pdf, dated 2026-04-20) covering 26 allergens over hundreds of rows — but it is a graphical table: the dash cells extract, the product names and the positive marks do not, so NOT ONE FLAG BELOW IS DRAWN FROM IT. Likewise the 温野菜の楽しみ方 page, which is where the broth choices are explained, is entirely images. So the broths and the dipping sauces were NOT read and are NOT described here; a coeliac must ask in the shop and should ask to be shown that PDF. What IS certain: raw meat, raw vegetables and mushrooms carry no wheat in themselves, so they are recorded ask rather than no; the wheat items are the noodles, and the 水餃子 wrapper. ⚠ NOTE THE DASHI COVER CHARGE: ordering only 単品 items costs 300 yen (税込330) per person おだし料金, free for under-sevens. ⚠ AND NOTE WHAT «60種類以上おかわり自由» REALLY MEANS: the all-you-can-eat courses differ only in how many CUTS OF MEAT are included (5 to 12), not in the vegetable side. Course length is 120 minutes, last order at 90.

tokyo_salad_cafe_keio_departme.price_note: EMPTY, AND THE FINDING IS THAT THIS BRANCH APPEARS TO BE GONE. The store URL on file returns HTTP 404 on the brand’s own site, and — more tellingly — Salad Cafe’s current お店をさがす page lists only two Tokyo locations, 東武百貨店池袋店 (Salad Cafe) and イトーヨーカドー武蔵境店 (皿多屋), alongside four Osaka shops. There is no 京王百貨店新宿店 anywhere in the operator’s live store list. The company (サラダカフェ株式会社) does publish brand-wide product pages by category — サラダ, デリカ, 弁当・パック商品, 美サラダ, ドレッシング — but attaching a chain product list to a branch the chain no longer lists would be exactly the cross-branch inference this project forbids, so nothing is recorded. This record probably needs verification of whether the shop still trades before it is researched again.
